newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank approves Italian cement deal.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank approves Italian cement deal.

text.p: Cyprus's Central Bank has approved the purchase by Italy's Italcementi of 13.2 million pounds ($28 million) of shares in Vassiliko cement, a representative of the Cypriot company said on Thursday.
The deal increases the Italian company's stake in Vassiliko to 33 percent of capital from the 20 percent it acquired in 1990. It is paying the Cypriot company 240 cents per share.
"After central bank consultations with the Finance Ministry and Commerce Ministry we received written approval yesterday," a Vassiliko official told Reuters.
Implementation of the deal is a matter of days, he added.
"We were obliged to approve the application before us based on our policy for foreign investments," central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou told Philelephtheros newspaper on Thursday.

The Central Bank vets all applications by overseas institutions seeking to invest on the island. Under Central Bank regulations foreign investors are allowed to hold up to 49 percent of capital in a local company, and 15 percent in banks.
The deal has been the subject of controversy and a heated parliamentary inquiry last week.

It was challenged by businessman Stavros Galatariotis's Cyprus Cement Company which said Cyprus's Greek Orthodox Archbishop Chrysostomos had reneged on a "gentleman's agreement" to sell Cyprus Cement the bulk of Vassiliko shares.
Chrysostomos is one of the largest shareholders in Vassiliko, which is controlled by the Hellenic Company Group.

Cyprus cement says it agreed with the Archbishop to buy 39 percent of Vassiliko shares at 209 cents -- but that deal was scuppered at the last minute when Italcementi came along with a higher offer. Earlier this week Galatariotis made another bid to buy Vassiliko shares, offering 245 per share.
